Subject: DRAFT — Correction to the daily takings and GST template: please check before filing

There is an error in the GST formula in versions 1.0, 1.1 and 1.2 of my daily takings template. If you used one of these versions to record GST-inclusive takings, please stop using it and check your figures before filing. If you have already filed, there are steps below.

I uploaded the corrected version, v1.3, on 8 November. It is available through the download link on the original post.

What went wrong

Column F multiplied the takings entered by 9%. That is correct for amounts excluding GST. It is not correct for amounts that already include GST. To extract the GST portion from inclusive takings, the formula should be:

GST-inclusive takings × 9/109

Ravi’s example makes the difference clear. His day’s takings were $1,090, including GST. The old template calculated $98.10 of GST. The correct GST is $90. That is an overstatement of $8.10.

This was my error. I tested v1.0 against my own sample figures, which were already excluding GST, so the check passed. I did not catch what happened when inclusive takings were entered. That explains how I missed it; it does not excuse it.

Who needs to check

The error affects people who entered GST-inclusive takings in v1.0, v1.1 or v1.2. That will include many hawkers recording the full amounts collected from customers. If your entries excluded GST, this particular formula error does not affect them.

There have been 412 downloads since the template was released on 12 August. I cannot tell from that how many people used it to file, so please pass this correction to anyone you shared the sheet with.

The quarterly Box 1 sales total was calculated independently and was correct in the affected versions. Column F and the resulting Box 6 GST figure were affected.

This error overstates GST; it does not understate it. Nobody underpaid IRAS because of this formula error. Some users may have overpaid and should check the correction route.

If you already filed Q3 using the sheet

1. Keep a copy of the original workbook and the return you submitted. Do not overwrite them. You will need a record of the figures used.

2. Check which version you used and whether the takings entered included GST. Check the receipts and records, not just how your menu prices were displayed.

3. Download v1.3 and use a separate copy to recalculate Q3 from the same records. Set H2 to match the amounts you enter. Select “prices exclude GST” only when the entries themselves exclude GST. For receipts including GST collected, use the inclusive setting, even if your menu prices exclude GST.

4. Compare the corrected quarterly Box 6 figure with the amount filed. Keep the calculation showing the difference. This formula error alone is not a reason to change Box 1.

5. Before making a correction, read IRAS’s “Correcting Errors Made in GST Return” page on iras.gov.sg and speak to the person who files your GST return, or IRAS if you file yourself. IRAS has its own rules on whether an error can go into a later F5 or requires a GST F7. Do not assume either route applies automatically.

If you have not filed yet, use v1.3 with the correct H2 setting and check the quarterly figures against your records before submitting.

Melvin is right to be upset. People trusted this sheet partly because I am an accountant, and they should not have had to catch this mistake for me. I am sorry for the extra work and worry it has caused.

Thank you, Ravi and Shu Fen, for spotting the problem and spelling it out. Please check your version and your input amounts before using the template again.
